appraisal_events.evidence: "Celles du second en avaient deux qui étaient vieilles et laides et qui s'appelaient Mme Verdurin et Mme Bontemps"; "Mme Bontemps avait été un peu dépaysée..." progressing to "avant la fin du premier mois... pas une duchesse ne se serait couchée sans avoir appris de Mme Bontemps ou de Mme Verdurin... ce qu'il y avait dans le communiqué du soir."
appraisal_events.explanation: Within a month Mme Bontemps rises from a disoriented social newcomer, mocked by Mme Verdurin's curt correction, to a source duchesses depend on for war news, though the narrator frames this ascent with comic irony (an 'old and ugly' queen of a second Directoire).

appraisal_events.evidence: "Maintenant qu'on voyait chez les Saint-Loup tous les gens 'qu'on connaissait', Gilberte aurait pu avoir les moeurs d'Odette elle-même que, malgré cela, on y serait 'allé' et qu'on eût approuvé Gilberte de blâmer comme une douairière des nouveautés morales non assimilées."
appraisal_events.explanation: The scandal of her marriage to Saint-Loup has fully dissolved; society now receives Gilberte unconditionally and would even back her in condemning others' unassimilated conduct, an elevation the narrator presents with irony at society's hypocrisy.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Vous viendrez entendre Morel. Or Morel n'aurait pas dû être là, pour la raison qu'il n'était nullement réformé. Simplement il n'avait pas rejoint et était déserteur, mais personne ne le savait."
appraisal_events.explanation: While touted as a draw of Mme Verdurin's salon, Morel is revealed by the narrator to be a deserter hiding in plain sight, a serious discrediting fact unknown to the company around him.

status_effects.explanation: She moves from a mocked newcomer to an indispensable wartime information source that duchesses rely on, even as the narrator's framing stays ironic.
Once a source of scandal, she is now fully and unconditionally included in society, even granted moral authority over others.
The narrator's exposure of his desertion is a serious moral discredit, even though it has no visible social consequence within the scene since it remains unknown to others.

ambiguities: Brichot's remark ('Dans ces temps préhistoriques') carries a faint ironic hint of nationalist amnesia/hypocrisy about his own dreyfusard past, but the passage does not develop this into a distinct local event, so he was omitted.
Saint-Loup's marriage is part of the same assimilation movement scored for Gilberte; a parenthetical aside about his earlier 'mauvaise pente' is too glancing to support a separate event for him.
